newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Megawati supporters protest at Indonesia parliament.
newsitem.headline: Megawati supporters protest at Indonesia parliament.

text.p: About 1,500 supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri protested outside national parliament on Tuesday in a show of strength for the ousted Indonesian minority party leader ahead of May's general elections, witnesses said.
They said the protesters unfurled banners saying "Mega or Nothing" and chanted "Mega Will Win".
Police with rattan sticks and bamboo shields blocked gates to the parliament building in central Jakarta but there were no incidents.
Three truckloads of armed soldiers were seen in the vicinity but were apparently being kept in reserve, the witnesses said.
Six military helicopters briefly hovered over the site of the protest but later flew away, they added.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, has been barred from running in the May 29 general elections.
She was ousted from the leadership of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government-backed faction last June.

The names of Megawati and her supporters were omitted from the list of election candidates supplied by the government-backed faction, which authorities have said represents the genuine wing of the party.
Indonesia only allows three parties to contest elections -- the PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party -- and all candidates must be approved by the government.

Jakarta was rocked by its worst riots in two decades when members of the government-backed faction stormed the PDI headquarters in the city in July and ousted Megawati supporters with the help of police.
At least five people were killed and 149 injured in the violence, the national human rights commission has said. A number of buildings were damaged and dozens of vehicles set on fire.
